sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: How does one very large value affect mean and median?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 29 yes, 8 no; row 2: 11 yes, 28 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 7x + 12, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional test points is associated with 7 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 7 test points.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 7 test points.
The predicted value is 7 test points when x is 0.

items.prompt: In a randomised trial, one group received a tutoring programme and scored higher on average than the control group. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.

items.prompt: A data set records 6, 2, 2, 2, 29, 18, 30. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 12.71, median 6
mean 6, median 12.71
mean 12.71, median 13
mean 13, median 6

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 169 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 40 yes, 7 no; row 2: 57 yes, 24 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 5x + 6, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 5 test points.
The predicted value is 5 test points when x is 0.
Each additional test points is associated with 5 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 5 test points.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.

choices: Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
